status_meaning: Source evidence, device reports, hypotheses and user-requirement gaps are separate. This document update does not implement any pending app fix.

issues.title: Recurring blank board / line drawing
evidence: User reports recurrence beyond the first app opening, including on iPhone 17 Pro Max.
Earlier attached screenshots show a top resize handle, top-right Delete and 123/Emoji bottom row unlike the reviewed AltBoard source.
User could not confirm the active keyboard name; said supposedly AltBoard.
Current source already removes cursor-mode letter fading and retains a bounded hosting root. Build 120 passes compile/package checks; this does not establish the cause or a device fix.

Supplied build-123 JSON has matching app/keyboard SHA d2fb55443e710ab492231073c9620de715f5eac9: 73 lifecycle events, 10 sessions, eight didAppear, two sessions ending after initial layout; zero recorded memoryWarning; nativeSwitchRequired false in all captured events. This does not establish termination or active pad ownership.
The supplied video visibly contains an ink pad in WhatsApp and Notes and ordinary Altboard letter keys between scenes.
Local main now contains the requested temporary Globe suppression and on-demand swipe drawing layer. No phone test or new IPA proves the recurring pad is resolved.
acceptance: Identify the selected keyboard by name while the failure is visible; do not infer selection from being inside AltBoard.
Explicitly select AltBoard; record whether keys return, stay blank or switch away again.
Check app/extension build stamps and any matching termination report; a historical probe or breadcrumb alone is not proof.
Repeat focus, keyboard dismissal/reopening, host switches and interrupted gestures in ChatGPT, Notes and the app test field; both key visibility and text insertion must work.
hypotheses_not_verified: Another active keyboard, possibly Apple Chinese handwriting
System fallback following an extension exit or memory termination
A remaining AltBoard rendering, layout or touch-lifecycle defect

issues.title: Meetings missing-model message names an obsolete settings path
evidence: MeetingRecordsView instructs Settings → History & Storage → Speech Recognition Models.
Current SettingsView puts Speech Model under Speech & AI; History & Storage has no model destination.
acceptance: In a separately authorized app patch, use the existing Settings → Speech & AI → Speech Model destination and matching localized help text.
Check the no-Qwen meeting action and all affected links; update the menu map. No app edit is included in this document update.

issues.title: Storage categories are coarser than the requested structure
evidence: Current LocalUserDataStore categories are voiceNotes, meetings and vocabulary.
Vocabulary combines Corrections & Suggestions. Export/Delete All Data keeps downloaded models and app settings.
The user requested model management plus separate manual-correction and learned-suggestion controls. This is not fully represented in current storage UI.
acceptance: Before an app patch, define exact data-category boundaries and existing storage consumers; preserve independent retention/export/deletion behavior.
Describe what each export/delete contains, preserve confirmations and active-recording guards, and verify unrelated categories survive.
Keep proposed menu changes separate from the current-source menu until implemented.

issues.title: Settings jitter and duplicate-flow regression acceptance
evidence: Current code groups Customization and removes haptic strength/test menus there; Active Session is on Settings home.
User reported jitter, redundant menus and repeated controls. Focused source checks pass; representative iPhone scrolling and navigation have not been verified.
acceptance: Test scrolling and expansion on iPhone 17 Pro Max, including returning from submenus and reopening Settings.
Confirm one Active Session toggle and one Customization group, persistent preferences and visible Preview.
If a UI audit is requested, present five evidenced problems and proposed changes before editing; do not infer smoothness from a build.

issues.title: Heretic feasibility, faithful Traditional Chinese and actual refusal behavior
evidence: Current source recommends 0.8B/2B/9B Heretic choices using language and memory policies.
9B MAX-MTP IQ3_M is approximately 5.72 GB on disk; current policy requires at least 12 GB physical RAM and 8.4 GB available app memory.
Recommendation is not active selection, existing downloads are not replaced automatically, and inference uses CPU without enabled MTP acceleration.
Prompt-contract checks pass; actual latency, memory behavior and political/historical rewrite results have not been tested.
acceptance: Confirm recommended, installed and selected model separately; test with the selected Heretic download.
Check meaning and Traditional Chinese preservation with the user’s historical/political rewrite example.
Measure cold/warm latency, available memory and interruption behavior on the phone; do not promise uncensored outputs or 9B viability from file size.

issues.title: Language Priority does not govern every language/model algorithm
evidence: Ordered selection and supported Latin suggestion boosts exist; local context may outweigh stored order.
Available language selection is broader than the supported swipe/prediction paths; Qwen speech uses auto-detection.
Passing ordering tests does not prove Japanese prediction or universal n-gram prioritization.
acceptance: Check stored order after reopening and supported suggestion ranking without overriding strong local context.
For future language work, state decoder/model capability and fallback separately; do not silently imply support from a selectable preference.

issues.title: Stale menu and weak cross-page development handoff
evidence: Previous SETTINGS-WORKFLOW-TREE.md described a Models tab, haptic strength/test menus and duplicate session controls.
It has been replaced locally by a menu rendered from the reviewed APP-STRUCTURE.json snapshot.

Root AGENTS.md and CHAT-DEVELOPMENT.md require a feature-first, bounded owner/consumer check and document maintenance. The checker invalidates changed mapped owners; it does not parse Swift or prove completeness.
acceptance: JSON parses; menu generation and check agree; source-owner fingerprints and declared anchors match.
A changed owner and an edited generated menu must each produce a failing check.
For new routes, update reviewed entries and fingerprints before regenerating. The user should not be asked to supply the menu tree again.
